source_title: Maharashtra Ordinance No. II of 2005 (7 May 2005), new Art. 51A; enacted as Mah. 32 of 2005 w.e.f. 7-5-2005
note: Maharashtra convention (Bombay Stamp Act 1958, Art. 51A(b)(i), delivery transactions): Rs 1 per Rs 10,000 = 0.01%. The rate before 2020 depended on the client's state; other states are not recorded here. Both sides: the SEBI FAQ on the 2020 reform says duty was payable by both seller and buyer before it (https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/faqfiles/dec-2021/1639980911330.pdf). Mah. 15 of 2011 would cut the delivery rate to 0.005% but its enforcement date is 'not yet declared' in Schedule I as modified to 1 Jun 2022 (https://ipindia.gov.in/storage/uploads/reference/AN5hvWq67hNPCYJHoo0pRTK5Y65qVagMexZo726B.pdf), so it is not applied. TaxRegimeParams.stamp_duty_rate is charged on the BUY leg only, so the sell-side duty of this period cannot be carried in the regime.

source_title: SEBI FAQ on Indian Stamp Act 1899 amendments (Finance Act 2019) and Rules: Q4 in force 1 Jul 2020, Q33 rate table
note: Uniform 0.015% on transfer of securities on a delivery basis, paid on one side only. The FAQ does not name the side for exchange trades; buyer-only is from broker notices (https://zerodha.com/z-connect/?p=241297 , https://zerodha.com/charges/ : 0.015% on the buy side, fetched 2026-10-23) and from the FAQ's rule that duty goes to the buyer's state.

source_title: SEBI FAQ on Indian Stamp Act 1899 amendments, Q2: levied on one side only
note: No stamp duty on the sell leg of an exchange trade since the uniform regime.

source_title: NSE/F&A/13028 (7 Sep 2009) Reduction in transaction charges, Capital Market segment
note: Flat Rs 3.50 per lakh each side, stated as the level 'presently' levied on the circular date. When this level began is not in any document found, so the row starts at the circular date.

source_title: NSE/F&A/13028 (7 Sep 2009), slab structure from 1 Oct 2009; NSE/FA/46730 (18 Dec 2020) lists Rs 3.25 as the existing rate
note: Lowest-turnover slab (up to Rs 1,250 crore traded value a month); a retail client's member slab is unknowable. Rs 3.25 per lakh each side. No intermediate NSE revision was located; the rate is confirmed at both ends by the two circulars (second: https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/circulars/FA46730.pdf). The Aug 2020-Sep 2022 Covid-era concession (https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/circulars/FA45147.pdf) excluded NIFTY 50 and NIFTY Next 50 constituents, so it does not apply to index stocks.

source_title: NSE/FA/46730 (18 Dec 2020) Revision in Transaction Charges, effective 1 Jan 2021
note: Lowest-turnover slab (up to Rs 1,250 crore traded value a month); a retail client's member slab is unknowable. Rs 3.45 per lakh each side; the increase was to augment the Investor Protection Fund corpus. Rolled back by NSE/FA/56129.

source_title: NSE/FA/56129 (24 Mar 2023) Revision in Transaction Charges, effective 1 Apr 2023
note: Lowest-turnover slab (up to Rs 1,250 crore traded value a month); a retail client's member slab is unknowable. Rs 3.25 per lakh each side. NSE/FA/73061 (https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/circulars/FA73061.pdf) says the member's IPFT contribution was raised by Rs 9.99 per crore each side from this date; that levy is not part of this rate and the schema has no field for it.

source_title: NSE/FA/61137 (14 Mar 2024) Revision in Transaction Charges, effective 1 Apr 2024
note: Lowest-turnover slab (up to Rs 1,250 crore traded value a month); a retail client's member slab is unknowable. Rs 3.22 per lakh each side. IPFT contribution as in the previous row.

source_title: NSE/FA/64232 (27 Sep 2024) Revision in Transaction Charges, effective 1 Oct 2024
note: Uniform Rs 2.97 per lakh each side for all members (no slabs) after SEBI circular SEBI/HO/MRD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2024/92. IPFT contribution of Rs 10 per crore each side is charged on top (NSE/FA/73061), so the total member outflow is Rs 3.07 per lakh.

source_title: NSE/FA/73061 (27 Feb 2026) Revision in Transaction Charges, effective 1 Mar 2026
note: Transaction charge Rs 306.99 per crore each side; the IPFT contribution falls to Rs 0.01 per crore, so the total outflow is unchanged at Rs 307 per crore. Confirmed as 'NSE: 0.00307%' on https://zerodha.com/charges/ (fetched 2026-10-23). No later NSE circular was found.

source_title: Finance (No.2) Bill 2004 explanatory notes (service tax): rate raised from 8% to 10%, Education Cess 2% of the service tax
note: Service tax on stock-broker service, rate shown including cesses. Whether it was charged on the exchange transaction charge and the SEBI fee is disputed: a CBEC clarification reported by Taxmann (https://www.taxmann.com/datafolder/news/News9317.htm , not opened) added them to the brokerage, while CESTAT Ahmedabad held them not liable (https://www.taxscan.in/nse-bse-transaction-charges-sebi-turnover-fees-not-liable-service-tax-under-head-of-stock-broker-service-cestat/133148 , article of 22 Sep 2021). No dated rule was found, so the basis records only what is certain. 10% x 1.02 = 10.2%. Takes effect on enactment of the Finance (No.2) Act 2004 per the notes; the rate table gives 10 Sep 2004, so the row starts at the project's first regime date, 2004-10-01. The 10% level before April 2006 is also stated in the Budget 2006-07 memorandum (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2006-07/cen/dojstru2.pdf).

source_title: GST Council schedule of GST rates for services (14th meeting, 19 May 2017): all other services not specified elsewhere 18%; broker price list https://zerodha.com/charges/
note: GST on stock-broking services. Basis from the Zerodha charge schedule (18% on brokerage + SEBI charges + transaction charges, fetched 2026-10-23); STT and stamp duty are outside it. 1 Jul 2017 is the date service tax was replaced (secondary: https://www.allindiaitr.com/indian-tax/service-tax-rate). The 22 Sep 2025 GST restructuring did not change the 18% on this service per secondary sources (https://busy.in/sac-code-9971/ , not primary). An exchange notice reported by the Free Press Journal (30 May 2025) says SEBI's own fee has attracted 18% GST since 18 Jul 2022.
